chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Abū Baṣīr and Zurārah, who both said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

"Indeed, part of the completion of fasting is giving zakat, meaning zakāt al-fiṭrah, just as salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is part of the completion of salat. For whoever fasts and does not give the zakat, then there is no fast for him if he deliberately abandons it; and there is no salat for him if he abandons salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with it before salat. He said:
"He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord, then prays."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory charity, here referring specifically to zakāt al-fiṭrah
key_terms.الصَّوْمِ: the fast, specifically the Ramadan fast in this context
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: zakāt al-fiṭrah given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.تَزَكَّىٰ: purified himself, understood here in relation to giving the due charity
key_terms.تَمَامِ: completion or perfection of an act of worship

ai.seo_question: How does zakāt al-fiṭrah complete the fast in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that zakāt al-fiṭrah is part of the completion of the fast, just as invoking blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is part of the completion of salat. It supports this teaching by citing the Qur'anic order of purification before prayer, highlighting the legal and devotional importance of fulfilling both obligations deliberately and properly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2085 - It is narrated by Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Basir and Zurara, who both said that Abu Abdullah (as) said:

"Indeed, completing the fast includes giving Zakat, meaning Zakat al-Fitr, just as sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) is part of completing the prayer. For whoever fasts but does not pay the Zakat (al-Fitr), their fast is not accepted if they intentionally neglect it. Similarly, whoever prays but does not send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), their prayer is not complete.
Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has mentioned it (Zakat) before prayer, saying:
'He indeed is successful who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord (azj) and prays.' (Surah Al-A'la 87:14-15)
